title: paged-kv-cache: block allocator reuse and pinning + TTL optimizations
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: The paged KV cache block manager currently suffers from churn and memory fragmentation under mixed-length workloads and high-concurrency continuous-batching scenarios. This causes increased page eviction and extra memcpy/alloc cycles that inflate tail latency and per-token CPU overhead. Summary: Implemented allocator reuse for block allocations, stronger pinning semantics for in-flight requests, and a soft TTL-based eviction path to avoid thrashing hot prefixes. The change includes: 1) a small fixed-size slab reuse pool for recently freed blocks to avoid repeated device allocations, 2) pin counts and a light-weight pin->deferred-unpin transition to guarantee KV pages referenced by active batches are not evicted mid-request, 3) a TTL-based mark-and-sweep soft-eviction that prefers cold pages but can be bypassed for low-memory fast-paths, and 4) telemetry hooks to emit block churn, pin contention, and reuse-hit metrics. Performance: internal perf-canary runs show 8-18% reduction in median token latency and 12-30% reduction in CPU token cost on mixed LLM traffic (sequence lengths 16-2048) on a 4xA100 configuration. Tail (p99) latency improved up to 24% in heavy concurrent continuous-batching tests. Tests & CI: Added unit tests for allocator reuse logic, integration tests simulating concurrent pin/unpin, and end-to-end perf harness scripts. CI: all unit/integration checks passed; one flaky benchmark job re-run and stabilized. Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind runtime.paged_kv.reuse_pinning; gradual rollout to dedicated pools for canary customers, monitor new/reuse_hit, pin_wait_time, and eviction_rate metrics. Related: follows up on prior paged-KV PRs (see pr-42789, pr-41290) and addresses incidents logged in SUP-7421. Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] integration tests, [x] perf harness, [x] docs inline, [x] metrics emitted, [x] feature flag. Notes: conservative defaults keep slab size small to avoid over-reservation; soft-TTL default is 5 minutes but configurable per-customer.

review_comments: Ethan Cole: Can you add a comment describing the invariants around deferred-unpin? I want to be sure we won't leak pins across task cancellations.
Maya Patel: Added detailed doc comments and a unit test that simulates cancellations which asserts pin counts decrement in all code paths.
Riley Zhang: Bench numbers look good — did you try workloads with very small sequences (<=8) where batching is aggressive? We should ensure reuse pool doesn't regress minimal sequences.
Maya Patel: Added an additional micro-benchmark for tiny-seq workloads; no regressions observed. Also added a config knob to scale slab reuse by workload profile.
Priya Nair: CI flagged a race in the TTL walker; suggest switching to an epoch-based scan to avoid locking hot paths.
Maya Patel: Reworked the TTL walker to epoch-snapshot and reduced lock hold times; pushed fix in commit f1b3c9a.
release_notes: Paged KV cache: block allocator reuse and pinning optimizations reduce token latency and CPU cost; adds soft-TTL eviction configurable per deployment.
merge_summary: Squashed 6 commits into main. Feature gated; telemetry added for safe rollout.
monitoring_playbook: Monitor metrics: paged_kv_reuse_hit_rate, paged_kv_pin_wait_ms, paged_kv_eviction_rate. If pin_wait_ms > 50ms for sustained 5m window, roll back flag or increase slab size. If reuse_hit_rate < 5% after rollout, consider tuning slab_size and workload profile.
notes: Backwards compatible; defaults conservative. Opt-in rollout recommended for high-throughput dedicated pools.
